key: Fight in the way of Allah against those who fight against you, but begin not hostilities. Lo! Allah loveth not aggressors.
s: The verse opens the ayahs commanding the believers to fight, slay and drive out those who fight them; al-Tabari, on 2:190, takes it as unrepealed, binding against the unbelievers’ fighting men, and reads the forbidden aggression as killing women, children or those who pay tribute.

evidence.words: وأولى هذين القولين بالصواب، القولُ الذي قاله عمر بن عبد العزيز. لأن دعوى المدَّعي نَسْخَ آية يحتمل أن تكون غيرَ منسوخة، بغير دلالة على صحة دعواه، تحكُّم … وأمرهم تعالى ذكره بقتال مَنْ كان منه قتال من مُقاتِلة أهل الكفر دون من لم يكن منه قتال من نسائهم وذراريهم … فمعنى قوله:"ولا تعتدوا": لا تقتلوا وليدًا ولا امرأةً، ولا من أعطاكم الجزية من أهل الكتابَين والمجوس
evidence.gloss: The sounder of these two views is the one ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz held (that the verse is not repealed), since to claim that a verse which may well be unrepealed has been repealed, with no proof of the claim, is arbitrary … And He commanded them to fight those who do fight, of the fighting men of the unbelievers, not those who do not fight, their women and children … So the meaning of ‘and do not transgress’ is: do not kill a child or a woman, nor any who have given you the jizya (tribute) of the people of the two Books and the Magians.

reason: The problem holds. Re-opened packet.js quran 3 --verse 2.190. After preferring ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz’s view that the ayah is unrepealed, al-Tabari paraphrases it in his own voice: fight in God’s way and call to His religion those who turn from it until they return to obedience or give the jizya, and God commanded them to fight those who fight, of the fighting men of the unbelievers (muqatilat ahl al-kufr), not their women and children. So the line he draws is combatant and non-combatant, and the old sentence, beside a context clause saying ‘those who fight them’, left him holding a standing command against attackers only. The reading now names whom the unrepealed command binds against (the unbelievers’ fighting men) and keeps his gloss on the forbidden aggression. The critic’s ‘holds’ is not an allowed verb, so ‘takes it as unrepealed’ is kept, and ‘ayahs that command’ became ‘ayahs commanding’ to stay within 45 words; plain sense otherwise unchanged. Commentator, place and src unchanged. Evidence: three verbatim runs from the packet joined with ellipses. verse.js ok (Al-Baqarah 2:190, at 196); entry-check ok.
